one_line_summary: The straight-leg, button-fly, 100% cotton jean that Levi Strauss has been making since 1873 and that essentially every other jean references.
energy: American canon — the jean that doesn't need to convince you of anything
pull_quote: Buy if you want one jean that ages into your body and doesn't go out of style. Pass if you need stretch, prefer a high rise, or have a curvy hip-to-waist ratio that the 501 won't accommodate.

verdicts.label: vintage / honest / Americana
verdicts.reasoning: This is the jean. 100% cotton means they age into your specific body — fade patterns develop where you bend, stretch where you sit. The mid rise and straight leg are flattering in a way trend-cuts can't be. Buy them in the medium wash and wear them for ten years.

verdicts.label: fitted / shaped / contoured
verdicts.reasoning: The 501 is cut straight from waist to hip with no curve allowance. If your waist is 6+ inches smaller than your hips, you'll have constant waistband gap or thigh pinch. Try the 501 Skinny or the Wedgie Straight (Levi's curve-cut alternatives) or look at Mother Tomcat for the same silhouette with curve-cut intelligence.

verdicts.label: tucked-in / waist-defining
verdicts.reasoning: The 501 is mid-rise. Specifically. The marketing calls it 'classic rise,' but it sits at the navel, not above. If you've been wearing high-rise for the last five years, these will feel too low. Try the 501 '90s instead (same brand, higher rise) or the Ribcage.

verdicts.archetype: denim purist / want the canonical pair
verdicts.label: honest / unprocessed / forever
verdicts.reasoning: These are the source. Every selvedge fan, every vintage collector, every denim head started with 501s. The Shrink-to-Fit version (sold unsanforized — they shrink ~10% in first wash) is the connoisseur pick. The standard sanforized version is what most people should buy.

why_people_love_it: 100% cotton means real fade patterns over years — the longer you wear them, the more personal they become
Mid rise + straight leg is the most-imitated silhouette in denim because it works on the widest range of bodies — but few brands execute it as well as Levi's
Genuinely affordable at $98 — most jeans this well-made are $200+
where_it_falls_flat: 100% cotton means initial discomfort — break-in takes 2-3 weeks of regular wear before they soften
Sizing runs vintage / true — waist measurement is the actual measurement, not the modern 'vanity sizing.' Check the chart, don't assume
Levi's currency is denim consistency, but specific washes do come and go — if you find one you love, buy two

alternatives.name: Levi's 501 '90s
alternatives.reasoning: Same brand, same fabric philosophy, higher rise and slightly slouchier through the leg. Better if you've been wearing high-rise and want the 501 DNA without lowering your waist.

alternatives.name: Mother Tomcat
alternatives.reasoning: Straight-leg with curve-cut intelligence. The waist is engineered for hip-to-waist ratio variance the 501 ignores. Twice the price but the fit improvement is real.

alternatives.name: A.P.C. Petit New Standard
alternatives.reasoning: Slimmer straight cut, Japanese selvedge, raw indigo. The Levi's of someone who wants their jeans to develop more aggressive fade patterns over time.
